Global Chess League: Carlsen’s Pipers Take the Lead
rubriker._rss_content: The Alpine APL Pipers, with Magnus Carlsen on the icon board, took sole lead in the standings on day three of the Global Chess League in Bengaluru. In their first match of the day, Carlsen beat Viswanathan Anand on time (pictured), but the Pipers nevertheless lost to the PBG Alaskan Knights. Carlsen's team then bounced back with a 15-3 victory over the previously leading FYERS American Gambits. After four of ten matches, the Pipers lead the table with nine match points, followed by four teams on six. | Photos: Global Chess League

rubriker.title: Philidor at 300: Chess Master, Musician and Pioneer
rubriker._rss_content: François-André Danican, better known as Philidor, was born 300 years ago today. A celebrated musician and the greatest chess player of his age, he made his living from chess in Paris and London, performed blindfold exhibitions in Berlin and, at the invitation of Frederick II, visited Sanssouci Palace. A look back at the remarkable life of one of the first great names in chess history. | Picture: François-André Philidor (1726–1795) by Augustin de Saint-Aubin and Charles-Nicolas Cochin

rubriker.title: ¿Cuán rápidas son las supercomputadoras de hoy?
rubriker._rss_content: A principios de la década de 1980, cuando apenas comenzaba mi carrera como periodista de televisión, hice un reportaje sobre la computadora más rápida del mundo. La Cray-1 costaba ocho millones de dólares y podía realizar 130 millones de operaciones de punto flotante por segundo. Eso era suficiente para calcular el tiempo, pero también para ganar dos campeonatos mundiales consecutivos de ajedrez por computadora. ¿Cuánto más rápidas son las supercomputadoras de hoy? Intenta adivinarlo: definitivamente no vas a acertar.
